biography: Zane Smith, a name once whispered with reverence in the Stock USA Gen3 circuit, hails from the dusty backroads of Oklahoma. His journey began not on asphalt, but on dirt, tearing through cornfields in a beat-up pickup his grandfather gifted him. The raw, untamed feel of the vehicle resonated with Zane, sparking a lifelong passion. At 19, he scraped together enough winnings from local dirt track races to buy a used Stock USA Gen2 car, and his meteoric rise began. He dominated the regional circuits, earning a reputation for fearless overtakes and unwavering composure. His breakthrough came at the '24 Oklahoma Showdown,' where, despite starting at the back of the grid due to a pre-race engine issue, he clawed his way to victory in the final lap. However, the transition to the Gen3 era has been challenging. While his steady hand still shines, the increased reliance on electronic assists hasn't suited his natural, seat-of-the-pants style. Now at 35, whispers of retirement are growing louder as he struggles to adapt.
drivingStyle: Zane's driving style is a throwback to a purer era of racing. He relies heavily on instinct and feel, preferring to manhandle the car rather than depend on electronic aids. He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the limits of grip. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also leads to inconsistencies, particularly in the technologically advanced Gen3 cars. He struggles with tire management, often overdriving early in the race, leaving him vulnerable in the final stages.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of worn-out cowboy boots to the track, believing they bring him good luck.
Listens to classic country music (specifically Johnny Cash) on repeat before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, claiming it jinxes his performance.
famousQuote: "Racing ain't about the fancy computers or the perfect simulations. It's about heart, grit, and the will to push harder than the next guy."
careerHighlight: Winning the '28 Stock USA Championship' after a season-long battle with Ricardo Alvarez. He secured the title with a dramatic last-lap pass at Homestead-Miami Speedway.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the '31 Daytona 500' while leading on the final lap. The devastating wreck cost him a guaranteed victory and severely impacted his confidence for the remainder of the season.
